items.note: Frame.io's how-to articles describe the same work: workspaces, internal and restricted projects, restricted folders, and permissions that cascade from a workspace to its projects and folders. Two details the scope could name if wanted: restricted projects (they break inheritance, so only people invited directly see them) and the rule that a permission cannot be lowered below the one a user inherits. Restricted projects are on the Team plan or higher, the Workspaces page in Account Settings is for Enterprise customers, and restricted folders are a V4 feature, so an Enterprise V4 account covers all of it. Keep Access Groups and synced Adobe user groups out of this line: both sit under a Group (Beta) tab.

evidence.quote: If a user is set up with permission on a Workspace, it will also cascade down to all internal Projects within the Workspace.

For example, if a user has Full Access on a Workspace, you cannot lower their permissions to Comment Only within an internal Project by assigning those permissions since the Full Access permissions still inherit downward.
Restricted projects are only visible to people directly invited.

Restricted Folders in Frame.io V4 are secure folders created within your Projects that are accessible only to explicitly invited Project Members, allowing for greater privacy, granular member control, and tighter security on the folders and assets you manage.
Note: This feature is for users on a "Team" plan or higher.
Note: This feature is only accessible to Enterprise customers.

To create a Synced User group, open your Account Setting, go to the Group (Beta) tab, click New Group , and select Add Adobe User Group .

items.note: Branded share pages, a default share template, passphrases, link expiry and download defaults are confirmed; the account-wide defaults sit on the Content Security page, which only Enterprise customers have. The correction is the last item: limiting shares to chosen domains is the Require Authorized Domain setting, part of Secure Sharing, and Frame.io's Secure Sharing article says Secure Sharing is supported for Enterprise Prime accounts only. The line carries no tier today, so the domains part should be worded as plan dependent, or the line should say Prime is needed for it. Note that Frame.io is not consistent: its Shares article calls secure sharing exclusive to Enterprise customers without naming Prime, and its pricing overview lists Secure sharing under Enterprise. Share Lists (saved reviewer lists, Pro plans and above) carry no label and could be named; Inbox carries a Beta label and must stay out.

items.note: The tier claim holds: Frame.io says session-based watermarking, forensic watermarking and Digital Rights Management are each supported for Enterprise Prime accounts only, and static watermark templates work on Enterprise Select and Prime, so the scope's 'where the plan includes them' is right. Things to add as prerequisites: forensic watermarking and DRM cover video only; a forensic investigation needs your client's own NAGRA NexGuard account, which Frame.io does not set up; downloads switched on for a share bypass DRM; watermark templates are created by Account Owners, Content Admins and Workspace Admins. Two limits a partner should know: content security settings do not protect assets in Workfront-linked projects, and Mounted Storage (Frame.io Drive) does not support watermarking, forensic watermarking or DRM. The watermarking article contradicts itself on static watermarks (one sentence says Enterprise Select and Prime only, another says all Enterprise, Team and Pro plans) and also calls session-based watermarking an add-on purchase; neither changes the line for an Enterprise client. No beta or similar label on any of these features.

Your client's own NAGRA NexGuard account before any forensic watermark investigation: Frame.io cannot run the detection
Downloads switched off on shares that rely on Digital Rights Management, because downloads bypass it

items.note: Frame.io documents custom metadata fields as the scope describes: a New Field option with 10 field types, fields kept in an account library and applied account-wide or to chosen projects, and a Fields Management tab that only admins see. No plan limit is stated for custom fields and there is no beta or similar label. By default Admins and Full Access users can create fields; admins can restrict it to Admins Only, which is a governance decision the service can include. Two cautions: the two articles give different counts of built-in fields (32 and 33), so do not quote a number; and custom fields do not travel to AEM Assets in the direct export (see frameio-aemassets).

evidence.quote: To make a new custom field, click the New Field option and you'll see 10 different field types to choose from.

Custom fields can be applied account-wide, meaning that even if a field is created within or for a specific Project, it could be used in any Project or Workspace in the account it was created in as well.
Custom metadata fields are now stored in an account library, which can be found in the Fields Management Tab in your Account Settings.
Note: This functionality is available to Admins and Full Access users by default, but can be adjusted by Admins in Account Settings to be Admins Only.
You can also manage and create your own custom fields.

items.note: Yes: Frame.io documents a direct export from Frame.io to AEM Assets that does not go through Workfront. It needs a Frame.io V4 account managed in the Adobe Admin Console, AEM Assets as a Cloud Service version 2026.07 or newer, and a Frame.io account admin to switch on the Adobe Experience Manager app on the Apps page in Settings. No Frame.io plan is named. Steps: an admin enables the app; a user with download permission in the project selects assets, then Actions > Export Assets; signs in to Adobe if asked; picks the Experience Manager repository; picks the folder; clicks Export; a success notice links to the assets in AEM. Limits: under 100 assets and folders and under 30GB per export, and Frame.io metadata is not sent. Frame.io itself says Workfront customers usually do better with the Workfront route because of its metadata mapping, so the existing XJ17 and XJ18 stay right for Workfront clients; the direct export fits clients who work mainly in Frame.io. The connection's 'how' sentence should drop 'which this session could not read'. No beta label on the export; the only forward-looking wording is on metadata transfer, which must not be offered.
items.proposed_how: Two routes. With Workfront: assets that finished review and approval in Workfront with Frame.io are pushed from Workfront, with their metadata, to AEM Assets as a Cloud Service; that integration is set up in Workfront and needs Adobe cloud storage. Without Workfront: once a Frame.io admin switches on the Adobe Experience Manager app, people with download permission export assets and folders from a Frame.io project straight into a chosen AEM Assets repository and folder, without Frame.io metadata.

items.note: Frame.io confirms the behaviour and adds detail the scope should use. Every new Workfront project creates a Frame.io project; by default it lands in one workspace called Workfront Linked Projects, to which users cannot be invited, in which standalone projects cannot be created, and which cannot be deleted. A Workfront project template can instead send its projects to another Frame.io workspace, which is the real design decision for a partner. Linked projects are always Restricted Projects; access is set only in Workfront (Manage and Contribute map to Edit & Share, View to Comment Only); assets uploaded on either side are mirrored; project, file and folder names must be unique; comments do not sync between the two products; projects cannot be moved between Frame.io workspaces later; Frame.io content security settings do not protect assets in linked projects. Requirements on the Frame.io side: a V4 account managed in the Admin Console, a Frame.io Enterprise agreement and Frame.io licenses for the people who work in the projects. The overview carries an eligibility line and a 'more features coming soon' line, but no beta label on linked projects themselves.
items.proposed_scope: Set up how your client's creative teams work in Workfront-linked projects in Frame.io: which Frame.io workspace each Workfront project template creates its projects in, who uploads where, how project, folder and file names stay unique, and how project sharing is handled from Workfront.

items.note: help.frame.io does not mention Adobe Express on any English page. The JSON's express-frameio connection (through Workfront unified review and approval) rests on Adobe's Workfront guide and nothing on Frame.io's site adds to or contradicts it.

The JSON names Premiere Pro only. help.frame.io documents more, none under a beta label: (1) Premiere: the Frame.io V4 panel is built into Premiere 25.6 and later (browse and import, upload sequences, versions, share links, comments synced to timeline markers), V4 accounts only; the JSON's 'review in the Premiere Pro timeline' is right but does not say V4 only. (2) After Effects: a native Frame.io V4 panel (render and upload from the Render Queue, share links, comment sync), V4 accounts only; missing from the JSON. (3) Lightroom: a Frame.io V4 project connects to a Lightroom account from the C2C Connections tab, automatic for Camera to Cloud images or manual with Send to Lightroom, images only, one way; missing from the JSON. (4) Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Media Encoder, Premiere and After Effects: no panel, but Frame.io Drive mounts a project as a drive so files open and save from the apps, each save making a new version; a Content Admin switches Mounted Storage on per project and each plan has a Mounted Storage allowance (2 TB on Enterprise); watermarking, forensic watermarking and DRM do not apply to mounted storage. (5) InDesign files are viewed and commented in Frame.io natively. Reported only; no service added.
